key_insight: The paper shows that unified multimodal models can learn to "think while repairing" their own image outputs by interleaving reflection and reinforcement learning. This joint training helps the model discover better self-correction paths than supervised reflection alone.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of training a model to diagnose flaws in an image, revise the image, observe the result, and reflect again when the usefulness of each revision is only known after rendering.
method: Use supervised fine-tuning on reflection trajectories to provide an initial cold start for the model.
Train the reflection text generator and image generation loop jointly with reinforcement learning so the model can learn from the success of full repair trajectories.
Interleave reflection, image generation, and feedback signals to optimize for higher-success self-revision paths rather than fixed offline examples.
impact: This matters because it improves the ability of multimodal models to self-correct, which can reduce manual iteration in image generation workflows. For practitioners, it offers a path toward more reliable, adaptive, and autonomous creative models.

paper_title: Learning Native Reflection in Unified Models with Interleaved Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Yijia Fan, Ziqi Huang, Zhongang Cai, Yan Li, Zimo Wen
